title: YouTube Library
summary: A YouTube attention tracker whose older 214,888-video backup exposed about 52,208 hours of remaining viewing—roughly 143 years at one hour per day.
epitaph: It counted the queue until the queue stopped pretending to be a plan.
revive_when: A deliberately bounded, deletion-first tool needs to expose the lifetime cost of saved media before it admits more.

related.reason: Problem Space could reverse the tracker’s accumulation model: retain a video only when it supports an active problem, using context as a filter rather than creating another comprehensive queue.

origin: User supplied the local old-repos-to-grave/youtube-library directory for burial on 2026-09-13, then added an older ZIP backup and asked that secrets, databases, and individual app data be excluded. The user reports that the tracker later held about 1.3 million videos and was abandoned after the scale of unwatched content made the premise feel pointless. The backup contains 1,194 channel records and 214,888 video records in two large JSON files. The caretaker inspected it statically in a temporary directory, retained only anonymous aggregates and schema-level observations, and preserved neither the archive nor its private records. No collected code was available or executed.
